profile.what: Palo Alto Networks is one of the largest cybersecurity companies, selling network firewalls, cloud security and security-operations software to large organisations. It has grown through frequent acquisitions.
profile.money: Most revenue is subscriptions and support that renew each year; firewall hardware is a shrinking share. Its strategy is to persuade customers to replace many separate security tools with its platform.
profile.valued: Investors value it on free cash flow and on growth in recurring revenue, not on reported earnings, which are held down by stock-based pay and acquisition charges. The debate is how much of that stock pay should count as a cost.

summary.sentence: A security platform consolidating its customers' tools, with cash flow far ahead of reported earnings.
strengths: Free cash flow is far above reported earnings.
Revenue has grown every year in the record.
Customers are consolidating onto fewer security vendors.
risks: Stock-based pay takes a large share of cash flow.
Share count rose sharply over the past year.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow: $2.3B a year: free cash flow less stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 9–15% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 7%; cost of capital 10.7%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
